name: Ironband's Excavation Site
summary: Prospector Ironband’s dig lies south of the Loch, where troggs have driven the miners from their trenches. The excavation in southeastern Loch Modan, southwest of Farstrider Lodge, has been halted.

sections.title: Unearthing the Past
sections.body: Prospector Ironband’s dig in southeastern Loch Modan began with a search into the dwarves’ ancient Titan origins. The work ended in disaster when the miners disturbed an unusually fierce, large breed of subterranean troggs. The creatures surged from the earth, drove the miners back, and made camp among scattered tools, broken carts, and half-excavated relics.

sections.title: Ruins in the Red Earth
sections.body: The troggs hold the site, while surviving prospectors wait at the edge of the perimeter. Like efforts in the Badlands, Wetlands, and Uldaman, this dig is caught in danger. The prospectors hope to reclaim their stolen gear and guard exposed artifacts, including strange ancient statues left by long-forgotten builders, from the ravenous troggs.

faq.q: Where is Ironband's Excavation Site located?
faq.answer: Ironband's Excavation Site lies in southeastern Loch Modan, directly south of the Loch and southwest of Farstrider Lodge.
Prospector Ironband is an archaeologist and explorer leading the excavation for the dwarven Explorers' League. He is trying to salvage artifacts and drive back the local troggs.

faq.q: Why is the excavation site overrun with troggs?
faq.answer: The miners dug deeper into Loch Modan and broke into underground pockets inhabited by a large, aggressive breed of troggs. The troggs overwhelmed the workers and seized the site.

faq.q: What were the dwarves hoping to find here?
faq.answer: The dwarves hoped to find ancient Titan relics and stone ruins that could shed light on the ancestral origins of their race.

angles.text: For the Explorers' League, losing the dig is a stinging setback. Recovering ancient relics here matters to understanding dwarven heritage.
The quarry and open pits show how dwarves use heavy extraction techniques. Trogg hostility makes prospecting hazardous.
